findings.claim: Unlisted risk: `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml` offers the `kmctl-check` hook to other repositories with `language: python` (ADR 0022). pre-commit and prek install a python hook by installing the hooked repo's root (`pip install .` / its uv equivalent). After the move, the root is a virtual workspace with no build target, so any user who sets `rev:` to a post-move tag gets a hook that fails to install (setuptools fallback on a flat root with packages/, scripts/, tests/), or installs no `kmctl` entry point. The plan does not mention the file, no outcome touches it, and `test_pre_commit_hook_runs_from_another_repo` (integration) would fail at build time with no planned fix. Whether a fix exists is open: pre-commit has no subdirectory option for python hooks. This needs a spike before the plan is revised. Question: on the moved tree, can a `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml` hook with `language: python` (prek 0.5.5 and pre-commit) install and run `kmctl check` from a post-move commit, for example with `additional_dependencies: [./packages/kmctl]`, or does the root need a build target, which conflicts with `package = false`? If neither works, the operator has to accept that the hook ends (or changes shape) for post-move tags, like risk 2.

The Outcomes facts say O1 can ship alone, but it cannot. On its own, O1 moves src/kmctl into packages/kmctl. The editable install's `parents[2]` fallbacks then point at packages/kmctl, which has no apm/ (O3), so the skills, agents and rules tests fail. Root tests that cite `src/kmctl` paths break (O2). The release workflows' bare `uv build` fails at a root that installs nothing (O6), so main could not release, which the Intent says must keep working. O2 and O3 are `support` outcomes that no behaviour lists in `needs`, and O6 is a separate behaviour. plan.split could therefore cut O1 off from them and land a red tree. Make O1 need O2, O3 and O6's workflow path change, or fold them into O1, so the move lands as one unit.

Some `needs` entries leave out outcomes they wait on. O6 checks that ci.yml's starter job runs `packages/kmctl/tests/test_starter.py`, a path that only exists after O2, but O6 lists `needs: O1` only. O5 touches `tests/test_starter.py`, `tests/test_docs.py` and `tests/test_repo_name.py`, which O2 moves into packages/kmctl/tests, and O4 touches `tests/test_pin.py`, which also moves. Their touches and ordering depend on O2, but O2 is not in their `needs`.

P4 lists `scripts/release.py`'s install pattern dropping the `#subdirectory=` fragment. O6, the only outcome that fixes P4, does not touch release.py. O5 does touch it and checks it (`release.py set` keeps the fragment), but O5 lists only `fixes: P2`. Either O5 also fixes P4, or the release.py part of P4 belongs in P2.

Settled by spike:kmctl-to-packages/5: additional_dependencies ./packages/kmctl plus a hatchling empty-wheel root build-system installs and runs kmctl-check in prek 0.5.5 and pre-commit 4.7.0, and uv sync --locked still installs no root package. O1 now carries it.
The tests move, apm fallbacks, release workflow builds and hook are now folded into O1. The remaining gap (action.yml and the starter) is a different fact, raised as p5.
O2, O3 and O4 each need O1, which now holds the test move.
release.py's fragment now sits in P2, which O3 fixes.

O1 still cannot ship alone: two pieces it waits on sit in O3. (a) action.yml:142 runs `uv tool install "${{ github.action_path }}"`, the root. After O1 the root builds only the empty hatchling wheel (risk 4's fix), so that install gives no kmctl executable and fails. ci.yml's `knowledge` job (`uses: ./`) is the job every other CI job `needs`, so O1 alone leaves all of CI red. (b) O1's checked-by has ci.yml's starter job running packages/kmctl/tests/test_starter.py -m integration. That test bootstraps a generated project whose justfile runs `uv tool install git+...kmctl@REF` against a file:// clone of the moved tree, which needs starter/justfile.jinja's fragment, an O3 change. Move action.yml and the starter's kmctl_src into O1 (or make O1 need them), so plan.split keeps them together.

The v0.12.1 cutoff breaks the two integration tests that install this tree from a tag. tests/conftest.py:122 `tree_repo` tags the copied working tree `v{version('kmctl')}`, which is v0.12.1 (apm/apm.yml:10) until the next release bumps it. tests/test_starter.py (TAG = v0.12.1, copier's kmctl_ref default) and tests/test_pin.py:339 (pin at TAG) then install `git+...@v0.12.1` from a clone whose v0.12.1 tag points at the moved tree. The plan's rule gives v0.12.1 no fragment, so uv installs the root, which holds no kmctl, and both tests fail. That contradicts O1's and O3's checked-by (the starter integration job passes) and O2's. Nothing in the plan bumps the version. The plan needs a rule for the in-tree version: for example tree_repo tags a version above v0.12.1, the tests pass a newer kmctl_ref, or the version bumps to a pre-release in this ticket. Pick one before building, because it decides what the cutoff compares against.
Settled by spike:kmctl-to-packages/5; O1 carries the hook change.
The move, fallbacks, workflows and hook sit in O1.
O2, O3 and O4 each need O1.
release.py's fragment sits in P2, fixed by O3.
action.yml, starter/justfile.jinja and the starter test now sit in O1, with the knowledge job and starter bootstrap in O1's checked-by.

The chosen fix (tree_repo tags its copy one minor past apm/apm.yml, a test-only tag) still breaks the starter bootstrap test, because only the tag moves and the copy's version stays 0.12.1. The copy's copier.yml kmctl_ref default is still v0.12.1 (tests/test_starter.py:171 pins it to apm.yml's version), so copier renders kmctl_ref v0.12.1 and apm.yml/justfile ask the file:// clone for a tag it no longer has, and the install fails. If the test passes the new tag as kmctl_ref instead, apm.lock.yaml pins v0.13.0 while the installed CLI reports 0.12.1 (version comes from the copy's apm/apm.yml), so doctor's lock check fails (src/kmctl/doctor.py:373, resolved_ref != package_ref()), and test_bootstrap_installs_this_checkout asserts report['ok']. The tag and the copy's own version must agree: for example tree_repo runs `scripts/release.py set` (apm.yml files, copier.yml default, pinned lines) on the copy to the test-only version before committing and tagging, so the installed CLI, the lock, the copier default and the tag all say the same post-move version. State that rule in O1.

O1's checked-by says the pin integration test passes against the moved tree, but that test does not use tree_repo's tag: test_hands_off_through_a_real_uvx (tests/test_pin.py:335) writes a lock at OTHER = 'v0.5.1' (tests/test_pin.py:23) with the tree's commit and unsets KMCTL_PINNED, so it really hands off through uvx. On O1 alone pin.py has no fragment, so uvx builds the root's empty wheel and finds no kmctl; after O2 the rule gives v0.5.1 no fragment either, with the same result. So the pin integration test cannot pass in O1 and does not pass in O2 as written. Move that claim from O1's checked-by to O2's, and have the test pin a ref newer than v0.12.1 that differs from the running version (the hand-off is skipped when they match, pin.py:151). O1 should not claim it, or the integration gate stays red until O2 lands.
Settled by spike:kmctl-to-packages/5; O1 carries the hook change.
The move, fallbacks, workflows and hook sit in O1.
O2, O3 and O4 each need O1.
release.py's fragment sits in P2, fixed by O3.
action.yml, the starter justfile and its test ship with O1.

tree_repo now runs scripts/release.py set on its copy at the test-only version before committing and tagging, so tag, apm.yml files, copier default, the starter's lock and the installed CLI agree; set_version rewrites exactly those files and needs no git state.
The real uvx hand-off claim moved to O2's checked-by and pins tree_repo's test-only tag, which is newer than v0.12.1 and differs from the running version.

The plan gives the root tests/ its own small conftest with the autouse fixtures its tests still need (the per-run uv cache, KMCTL_PINNED). None was added. _uv_cache now lives only in packages/kmctl/tests/conftest.py, so the root integration tests that run uv (tests/scripts/test_check_wheel.py package_build, test_smoke_wheel.py, test_release.py's _build) write to the shared uv cache whenever they run without a kmctl test in the same session, which is the growth that fixture exists to stop.
